transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (AE), Priya Desai (SE), Liam O'Connor (CSM) — Solstice: Maya Lin (CTO), Andre Gomez (Dir Infra), Sofia Chen (Security), Rajat (DevOps), Elena (Legal)

Summary:
Redwood-led security kickoff to align on SAML/IdP integration, SCIM provisioning, RBAC role slices and least-privilege model, audit log retention and routing, and customer-managed key (CMK) options for encryption at rest. Customer priorities: EU data residency, SOC 2 evidence, minimal blast radius for service accounts, and cert rotation policies.

Topics: IdP metadata, SAML assertions & attributes, SCIM groups & mapping, RBAC role templates, audit log streaming to Splunk, KMS/CMK integration, data residency & Private deployment options, SOC2/ISO artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call please.
[00:06] Maya Lin: Hi, Maya here, CTO at Solstice.
[00:09] Andre Gomez: Andre, infra.
[00:11] Sofia Chen: Sofia, security.
[00:12] Rajat Patel: Rajat, DevOps.
[00:14] Elena Ruiz: Elena, legal.
[00:16] Jordan Park: Great. I'll hand off to Priya to run through the technical flow and then we can dive into SCIM and RBAC.
[00:22] Priya Desai: Hi all. High level — we want to confirm three things: how you want to connect your IdP to Redwood, how users/groups map into Redwood roles, and how you want logs and keys handled. I'm going to sketch an example SAML flow then SCIM mapping. Please stop me if anything sounds off.
[00:38] Priya Desai: For SAML, we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated. Assertion needs to include NameID (email) and we like to receive an attribute for role or groups, e.g., groups claim with full DN or a simple group array. Some IdPs send group IDs, some send names — either works but we need mapping.
[00:55] Andre Gomez: Quick question — we use Azure AD but have a proxy in front that rewrites some claims. Will that break anything?
[01:02] Priya Desai: It can. If claims are rewritten you'll need to either change the rewrite rules to keep the group attribute intact or provide us a mapping table. For example if group claim is "grp_names" vs "groups" we'll map accordingly. We can accept multiple attribute names.
[01:18] Sofia Chen: On encryption — we require customer-managed keys for any workspace that touches PHI. Do you support CMK with rotation and KMS integration?
[01:26] Priya Desai: Yes, we support CMK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or optional Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) in supported regions; rotation is supported with a staged rewrap process. Note: the Private deployment path gives you full control over keys via your KMS/HSM.
[01:44] Maya Lin: If we go hosted with BYOK, can we ensure the keys never leave EU?
[01:50] Priya Desai: We can pin key material to regional KMS endpoints — if you require EU residency we recommend Private or Dedicated in EU region. Hosted BYOK is possible in EU, but we need contractual language for residency guarantees.
[02:04] Elena Ruiz: We'll need that in the contract; also want SOC 2 evidence before any pilot.
[02:09] Jordan Park: Understood. We'll send SOC 2 bundle and ISO references after this call.
[02:14] Priya Desai: Switching to SCIM — we support group sync for automatic provisioning and deprovisioning. SCIM can be configured to sync group membership to Redwood roles. Typical pattern: SCIM group = RBAC role, with admin groups mapped to higher-perm roles.
[02:31] Rajat Patel: Our concern is blast radius. We have some CI service accounts that should not be admins. How do you carve those out?
[02:37] Priya Desai: Two approaches: 1) Use a dedicated service account OU in IdP that maps to a tightly scoped role in Redwood; 2) Use attribute-based mapping — e.g., an attribute 'serviceAccount=true' that SCIM sends so those accounts get a sandbox role. We can also exclude certain users from SCIM by filter.
[02:56] Andre Gomez: Filtering sounds ideal. Is filtering evaluated server-side or by our IdP?
[02:59] Priya Desai: Filters are on Redwood side during provisioning — we evaluate SCIM list endpoints or incoming patch operations and apply filters you provide. We log all provisioning events.
[03:10] Sofia Chen: About auditing — we need immutable logs for SSO events and admin actions, and ability to forward to Splunk. Retention 7 years for some artifacts. Is that supported?
[03:20] Priya Desai: We forward syslogs/events via secure streaming. Default retention in hosted is 90 days, but for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and export to your SIEM. 7-year retention typically requires you to archive externally — we can stream to an S3 bucket in your account or to your Splunk HTTP collector.
[03:37] Sofia Chen: Ok we'll probably archive to our S3 with lifecycle rules.
[03:40] Jordan Park: Note — we'll include an example Splunk HEC config and sample event schema in follow-up.
[03:47] Priya Desai: On RBAC design, we recommend role slices: Admin, Power-User (can run infer jobs), Viewer (read-only), Service (CI/service accounts). Keep number of roles small to reduce complexity.
[03:58] Andre Gomez: Can roles be scoped per team or per project?
[04:01] Priya Desai: Yes, we support role scoping at workspace and route level. For example "DataScience:Power" vs "Infra:Admin". We also support least-privilege via policy templates that restrict API surfaces.
[04:13] Maya Lin: About policy templates — can we define a custom policy that prevents model deletion and restricts model rollout? We want to limit that to ops only.
[04:20] Priya Desai: Absolutely. We have policy primitives for model:create, model:delete, rollout:execute. You can combine them into templates and bind to groups.
[04:28] Rajat Patel: How do you handle SAML certificate rotation — if our IdP rotates certs every 30 days how smooth is the handoff?
[04:35] Priya Desai: We support metadata URL ingestion and offline metadata upload. For aggressive rotation, we advise setting up both old/new certs in metadata (IdP supports key rollover) or use metadata URL so we pick up changes. If you rotate daily, we can accept an automated push; otherwise manual update via Console/API.
[04:53] Elena Ruiz: Legal question — what data do you store in logs? Do we get PII?
[04:58] Liam O'Connor: We typically log identifiers (user id, email) for auditability but can mask or hash on request. We don't store raw PII in trace logs; sensitive payloads are redacted. We can provide a log schema doc.
[05:10] Sofia Chen: Will those logs include request payloads or model outputs?
[05:14] Priya Desai: By default we log metadata about the request (timestamps, user, route, model id, token count). Model outputs are not logged unless you enable debug/eval mode. For compliance, many customers disable output logging and only retain usage metrics.
[05:30] Jordan Park: Customer question — if we need SOC 2 scoping for Redwood's hosted offering, are there shared responsibilities?
[05:36] Priya Desai: Yes; Redwood's SOC 2 covers our controls for the service but you remain responsible for access management and secure usage in your account. We'll send a shared-responsibility matrix.
[05:46] Andre Gomez: We want to do a POC that demonstrates: SAML SSO, SCIM sync, RBAC least-privilege, and logging to our Splunk collector. How long to spin up a Dedicated sandbox in EU?
[05:56] Priya Desai: Typical start is 5–7 business days for dedicated sandbox in EU, assuming networking and infra approvals. Private on-prem is longer. We can do hosted test with EU region quicker if you accept Redwood-managed infra.
[06:10] Maya Lin: We need proof that keys are never exported for BYOK — what's the guarantee?
[06:14] Priya Desai: For BYOK we use envelope encryption; the KMS never sends key material to Redwood. Redwood only receives wrapped keys. In Dedicated/Private, keys can be in your KMS in your account so we never touch raw key material. We'll attach a technical note.
[06:28] Sofia Chen: On SCIM schema — can you accept custom attributes we use, like employeeType and orgSlice?
[06:34] Priya Desai: Yes, we map custom attributes. We suggest canonical names during mapping to avoid drift. We'll share a mapping template.
[06:40] Jordan Park: Quick aside — any competitors you considered?
[06:42] Maya Lin: We've looked at AuthFlow and CloudAIEndpoints; main gap was model-specific RBAC and audit granularity.
[06:49] Priya Desai: Noted. We'll highlight our per-route traceability in follow-up.
[06:54] Rajat Patel: How do we isolate internal staging workloads from prod? Do we need separate workspaces?
[06:59] Priya Desai: Best practice is separate workspaces with distinct VPC/subnets and KMS keys. That gives you strong separation for billing, logs, and keys.
[07:10] Andre Gomez: Is there automation for provisioning new project workspaces via API?
[07:13] Priya Desai: Yes, you can create workspaces via API and programmatically bind groups/roles via SCIM or the Redwood management API.
[07:18] Sofia Chen: For long-term audit retention, is streaming to our S3 enough for compliance?
[07:22] Priya Desai: Yes, streaming to your S3 with lifecycle set to keep objects is common. We provide event formatting docs so you can parse.
[07:29] Elena Ruiz: Who signs the Data Processing Addendum (DPA)?
[07:32] Jordan Park: Our legal team will sign the DPA. We'll attach a copy in the follow-up.
[07:36] Maya Lin: On the SCIM side, if we deprovision a user, how quickly does that revoke tokens and sessions?
[07:42] Priya Desai: Token revocation is near-real-time for interactive sessions; for long-running inference jobs we provide revoke hooks and job-level ACL checks. We invalidate session cookies and issue a revoke to active tokens. There can be short windows (seconds) but it's immediate in practice.
[07:58] Rajat Patel: Any limitations on number of SCIM groups? We have thousands and want to avoid hitting quotas.
[08:03] Priya Desai: We support large group counts; for scale we recommend delta sync (patch operations) instead of full list on every run. We'll share best practices doc.
[08:12] Sofia Chen: For role separation, can we require MFA for role elevation to admin?
[08:16] Priya Desai: Yes, we support admin elevation workflows that require step-up auth — integration with your IdP's MFA is supported.
[08:24] Jordan Park: Ok time check — we've got about 30 minutes left, any high-risk items we should surface now?
[08:31] Sofia Chen: Data residency and long-term logs are high risk, plus legal needs on DPA and contract language for residency. Also key handling if we go hosted.
[08:41] Priya Desai: Action-wise: we'll share SOC2 bundle, SCIM mapping template, Splunk HEC example, and a proposed pilot timeline for Dedicated EU sandbox. We'll also include a short KB on key rotation.
[08:53] Andre Gomez: For pilot, can we test a CMK rewrap cycle to see performance impact?
[08:59] Priya Desai: Yes, we can instrument a rewrap test in the sandbox. We expect small latency impact per rewrap but it's manageable. We'll include tokenized metrics from prior tests.
[09:10] Maya Lin: On rollback/fallback — if Dedicated capacity is unavailable during a canary, do you fallback to hosted model? We want deterministic routing.
[09:18] Priya Desai: We have routing policies: you can prefer Dedicated and fail closed or prefer Dedicated with fallback to hosted. For strict isolation you can set fail closed. We'll document tradeoffs.
[09:29] Jordan Park: Let's capture next steps and owners.
[09:32] Priya Desai: Action items recap — (1) Priya: SCIM mapping + sample CSV, (2) Jordan: SOC 2 + ISO links, (3) Redwood: Splunk HEC example and event schema, (4) Solstice: IdP metadata and cert cadence, (5) Solstice: list of admin/service accounts.
[09:50] Elena Ruiz: We'll also need standard contract language for EU residency and BYOK assurances. Add that to the list.
[09:58] Jordan Park: Will do. Any final questions?
[10:02] Sofia Chen: One last: can you produce a short runbook for emergency key rotation or key compromise?
[10:07] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll share a runbook with steps for rotation, revoke, and rewrap.
[10:12] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts within 48 hours.
[10:16] Maya Lin: Thanks, appreciate it.
[10:18] Meeting end."
